children: OTTAWA--Canada's economy grew at the fastest pace in about three years in the second quarter with a jump in exports, higher household spending and a recovery in business investment.

Gross domestic product, a broad measure of goods and services produced in the economy, increased 3.3% at an annualized rate in the April to June period to 2.524 trillion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of US$1.822 trillion, Statistics Canada said Friday. Market expectations were for growth of 3.5%.

The expansion, the strongest growth since the first quarter of 2023, marks a sharp acceleration after GDP rose an upwardly revised 0.3% in the first quarter and contracted 1.0% in the final three months of 2025.

Industry-level data for June showed that GDP rose a third straight month in June, increasing 0.3% to match the pace in May. That was slightly stronger than the 0.2% growth previously forecast by Statistics Canada.
The data agency provided an early estimate for July that suggests GDP was essentially unchanged month-over-month.
